note: Direct comparison of the Layer 1 popularity baseline against the Layer 2 ALS model, both evaluated on the same test set under the same protocol.
finding: ALS scores roughly 10x lower on Recall@10 and NDCG@10 than the plain popularity baseline, but recommends across ~135x more of the catalog (coverage@10: 1.05% vs 0.0077%) with marginally lower popularity bias. This is consistent with the corpus statistics from Phase 2: the median user has only 1 training event, leaving ALS very little signal to personalize from, while a fixed bestseller list wins on accuracy simply because it always recommends items with real test-period demand. The honest conclusion for this dataset is that collaborative filtering alone does not beat the popularity baseline on accuracy at this sparsity level -- personalization gains, if any, will need to come from the two-stage reranker (Phase 4) combining ALS's broader reach with explicit features, not from ALS alone.
